claims.text: Integrating ab initio descriptors with explicit defect and oxygen-impurity parameters into a machine-learning framework will improve conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed improvement applies in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
Traditional analytical conductivity models assume ideal, defect-free crystals.
The model will include features for defect-induced scattering, oxygen effects, temperature-dependent electron-phonon coupling, and local lattice distortions.
Transport from 0–200 K is dominated by quantum effects and impurity scattering.
Transport from 300–1200 K is dominated by phonon scattering.
The approach applies to both pristine HfNbTaTiZr and material containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen impurities induce local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect states and oxygen-induced local lattice distortions mediate changes in electron-scattering mechanisms across temperature.
Defects and oxygen impurities alter the local electronic structure and scattering processes.
Explicitly representing these defect and impurity effects will allow the model to capture the true temperature-dependent transport behavior.
The machine-learning model will predict conductivity with less than 5% error relative to held-out experiments in each temperature regime.
The machine-learning model will outperform existing analytical conductivity predictions.
Existing analytical models typically deviate from conductivity measurements by more than 5%, especially for oxygen-containing samples.
The approach is validated for oxygen concentrations up to 1 wt.%.
The approach is validated over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Applicability outside the specified oxygen concentration and temperature limits is uncertain.
A deviation greater than 5% from measured conductivity in either temperature regime will falsify the model's stated accuracy target.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the approach is already validated within the specified ranges, whereas the uncertainty and proposed held-out experiment state that further validation is still needed. The model is also described prospectively as something to develop.
